description: Who governs a Texas address or coordinate: county (with FIPS), whether it is inside city limits (which city) or inside a city's extraterritorial jurisdiction (ETJ, estimated from the statutory distance), the nearest city and distance, school district, groundwater conservation district or rule of capture, ERCOT load zone and likely utility, and the FEMA flood zone (100-year floodplain, floodway, 500-year floodplain, outside, or not mapped) with distance to the nearest 100-year floodplain, mapped wetlands on the spot and within half a mile (USFWS National Wetlands Inventory; free says yes or no, Pro adds type, acres and distance) and USFWS critical habitat within 5 miles, and whether it is in a Qualified Opportunity Zone (QOZ) now and from 2027 (Texas OZ 2.0 tracts). Use when someone asks if a site is inside city limits or ETJ, whether it is in an opportunity zone, whether it is in a floodplain or flood zone, whether there are wetlands or endangered species critical habitat, whether zoning applies, which county or school district a parcel is in, who permits water wells there, or wants the permitting picture before buying land.

address.description: Texas street address, e.g. '1201 Main St, Houston, TX'. Use this or lat/lng.

lat.description: Latitude (WGS84). Use with lng instead of address.

lng.description: Longitude (WGS84). Use with lat instead of address.
